newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 16.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 16.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

HAMBURG - Hamburg-based advertising agency Scholz & Friends says it aims to expand its international network and have a significant group role following its merger into the British-based Bates. The holding company for the enlarged company will thus not be called Bates but have a "neutral" name, Scholz says. Plans for a Scholz Moscow bureau are also progressing. (Reuter)

WALLDORF - DDB Needham in Germany, based in Duesseldorf, is to take over global corporate advertising for Bayer. Corporate design for the chemical giant was previously handled by Munich-based Publicis MCD. (Kress)

BERLIN - The Sat.1 commercial television channel has put the Hamburg-based Wilkens agency in charge of its advertising account following its move in February to cancel its contract with Jung von Matt, also based in Hamburg. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - German parliament passes legislation that will allow government regulation of the Internet and set the stage for the development of new multimedia services in business and entertainment. The law sets standards for child protection in cyberspace and defines which activities require regulation and which can be operated without any formal license or regulatory oversight. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - The owners of pay-television channels Premiere und DF1 are close to signing a cooperation pact, news magazine Der Spiegel reports. One element of the deal could involve a merger of their subscription TV activities into one group, with Leo Kirch, one of the main players, raising his stake in Premiere to 50 percent and placing his DF1 unit inside the newly-merged group. (Reuter)

BONN - Interior minister Manfred Kanther has urged public broadcasters to reduce the amount of violence shown on television. The call follows official statistics showing a 12-percent increase in crimes by children in 1996. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - A new study by the ARD public broadcaster shows that radio listening is on the increase following programme changes in the west of the country and a large increase in commercial radio across the east of the country. Overall some 54 million Germans say they listen to radio every day, with an average listening time of 177 minutes. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

DUESSELDORF - Mannesmann group sales in the first five months of 1997 rise 16 percent to 14.3 billion marks and earnings in the period improve further, with automotive, telecoms, and pipes and trading divisions contributing to the improvement. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Software group Beta Systems says shares for its initial public offering will be priced between 85 and 100 marks in a bookbuilding process. Beta Systems will offer up to 897,000 shares, each with a nominal value of five marks.(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - German carmaker Adam Opel AG, a unit of General Motors Corp, extends the contract of Opel managing director David Herman for five more years. Herman, 51, was named to head Opel in July 1992 and has spent most of the last five years battling rival Volkswagen AG over allegations of corporate spying by former GM executive Jose Ignacio Lopez when he defected to VW in 1993. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Ex-Nestle man Alfred Petrich, 48, joins
Munich-based brewer Paulaner Brauerei as board chairman for the parent company. Responsibilities include strategy, marketing and publicity. (Handelsblatt)
